newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shuttle to cart away Russian trash from Mir.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shuttle to cart away Russian trash from Mir.

text.p: The crew of Russia's space station Mir did some spring cleaning on the 11-year-old craft on Monday, loading garbage onto the U.S. space shuttle Atlantis, a NASA official said.
The U.S. shuttle, which docked at Mir on Friday, was to haul away used food containers, broken equipment and other trash that had accumulated aboard the space station.
"It's cluttered. There is no doubt about that," said Jim Van Laak, the deputy head of NASA's shuttle-Mir programme.
"You need to periodically clean up and an event like having the shuttle show up is an excuse to have a garage sale and get rid of all this stuff."
Among the items being returned to earth aboard Atlantis were:
- a burned-out oxygen generator responsible for triggering a recent fire that filled the space station with choking smoke;
- 44 empty food cartons, which had contained Russian delicacies such as canned fish and boiled cabbage;
- an acoustic guitar, which will be supplanted by a new electric instrument.
NASA officials said they were also considering a request from the Mir crew to dispose of discarded foam packaging and some 300 pounds of water thought to be tainted by antifreeze.
The water, which was condensed from the cabin air and is usually recycled, may be dumped overboard by the shuttle crew, mission operations director Lee Briscoe said.
Atlantis, which is due to undock from Mir Wednesday, will also cart away a total of 2,500 pounds (1,134 kg) of scientific experiment results and old gear in need of refurbishment.
Unmanned resupply ships were previously used to dispose of most of Mir's trash. Garbage was packed aboard them and they would burn up while reentering the earth's atmosphere.
Such flights have been cut back since the shuttle started visiting the station.
